requirement:
> `Finish by submitting your structured result in result. Exactly one accepted
> submission ends this call.`
rationale:
structural: The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp.description` quotes only the description text of the submission tool: "Finish by submitting your structured result in result. Exactly one accepted submission ends this call." It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation through a named interface. Any implementation that advertises the tool with this description text meets it, however the string is built or placed. So every clause is observable behavior, and no structural obligation needs implementation evidence.

The supplied roots are consistent with this. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#fn[submission_tool]` builds the `submit_result` `ToolDefinition` with exactly this description string. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[GraphSession<'_, '_, D>/Conversation]/fn[tools]` only inserts the supplied submission definition into the tool list. Checking the description text itself is a behavioral matter, left to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The requirement has one observable obligation: the published `submit_result` tool's description is exactly "Finish by submitting your structured result in result. Exactly one accepted submission ends this call."

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[published_tool_descriptions_match_the_contract]` covers it and carries a {test} reference to the subject. The test runs `ValidationContext::ask::<bool>` with a scripted agent. It captures the tool definitions in the first provider request and finds the one named `submit_result`. It then uses `assert_eq!` to compare that tool's `description` with the exact required string.

The string in the test matches the requirement text exactly, so a changed or truncated description would fail. No other behavioral obligation exists. The tool's argument shape and acceptance belong to the parent `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp` and the cited acceptance requirement, which this assessment does not cover.
